clue.text: Can resident regularly reveal porkies on TV show?

indicators.note: taken together these words ask for every other letter of the word porkies to be exposed

parts.note: taken as written
ER is the long-running American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: Asks whether an inmate tells regular lies on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, not a tin. PRIS comes from the odd letters of 'porkies', which is British rhyming slang (pork pies) for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for jail, so someone who lives in the can is an inmate of a jail.

clue.text: Lights in HMP Slade out around one

indicators.note: around tells us the jumbled letters sit on either side of the piece for one
out here means wrongly placed or disordered, so the letters of HMP Slade are jumbled

parts.note: a means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Lights are out around one in Slade, the fictional prison of the sitcom Porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: HMP (Her Majesty's Prison) Slade is the jail in Porridge, the BBC sitcom that is this puzzle's theme. 'Out' scrambles its letters to give HEDLMPS, and 'around' puts them round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlamps are the front lights of a vehicle.

clue.text: One messes up Godber's pants

indicators.note: pants as British slang means rubbish or badly done, so the name Godber is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer makes a mess of Godber's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lennie Godber is Fletcher's young cellmate in Porridge. 'Pants' looks like trousers but is the anagram signal; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodger does work clumsily, a botcher who makes a mess of the job.

clue.text: Escape? Never!

definitions.meaning: a breakout or flight, especially from a crime or jail
the exclamation '...!', meaning you cannot be serious

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a jailbreak and gets an incredulous reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a flight from captivity, and 'get away!' is a cry of disbelief.

clue.text: Pleased to fiddle, dropping skirts and bloomers

parts.note: pleased means glad

indicators.note: the skirts of a word are its outer edges, so its first and last letters are shed

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: Someone happily fumbling with clothing, letting skirts and underwear fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping skirts' removes the V and N at the ends of VIOLIN to leave IOLI. 'Bloomers' looks like old-fashioned knickers, but here it means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are flowering plants, and a bloomer is something that blooms.

clue.text: Cheats and rogue start to make up stories

indicators.note: rogue here describes the letters as behaving unpredictably, so they are rearranged
the start to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheats and a rascal begin to invent tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a noun for a cheat; it is the anagram signal. The anagram uses M (from 'start to make'), UP and STORIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Impostures are deceptions or frauds, acts of passing oneself off falsely.

clue.text: He wrote because one needs second volume

parts.note: as can mean because
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A writer explains that one needs a second book.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific author of science fiction and popular science.

clue.text: Terrible Harry Grout mostly with yours truly taking drugs

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so one group of letters surrounds another
to harry is to harass or disturb, so these letters are thrown about
mostly means most but not all of the name, losing its final letter

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, me
Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: Harry Grout, the prison's kingpin in Porridge, is in a dreadful state after joining the setter on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Grouty is Slade's crime boss in Porridge. 'Harry' is the anagram signal, not his first name. 'Mostly' trims the name, the anagram gives GRUOME, and 'taking' wraps it around the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrible or ghastly, which is close to terrible.

clue.text: See 2
Exploited, took drugs

definitions.meaning: the slang sense of having consumed narcotics

explanation.surface: Someone was taken advantage of and went on to take narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means taken advantage of; as slang it also means having taken illegal drugs.

clue.text: Cells turn to fix as drug dealt externally

indicators.note: externally says the jumbled letters go on the outside of the other piece
dealt as in dealt out like cards, so the letters are distributed in a fresh order
turn tells us the word for fix is read backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Cells turn to fixing as a drug is sold outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealt' turns AS DRUG into GUARDS, which goes outside ROOM (MOOR read backwards because of 'turn').
explanation.definitionFit: Guardrooms are rooms where military prisoners are held, so they serve as cells.

clue.text: Welcoming back to prison, more angry one might cause disturbance at night?

definitions.text: one might cause disturbance at night?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: sorer means more angry or aggrieved

indicators.note: the back to a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An inmate, angrier at being sent back to jail, might cause trouble at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who snores disturbs the sleep of others at night.

clue.text: Noted deliveries, Porridge set twice cracked up

indicators.note: cracked up as in broken into pieces, so these letters are reshaped
twice means the word set appears two times

explanation.surface: Porridge, the theme sitcom, collapses in laughter after two scenes are set up.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses PORRIDGE plus SET and SET (from 'set twice').
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent this way is recorded and signed for, so these deliveries are formally noted.

clue.text: Steal show outside, returning fruitless

indicators.note: returning means the whole combination is read backwards
outside says the show surrounds the word for steal

parts.note: Evita is the musical
to steal is to rob

explanation.surface: Someone plans to steal a show, but it comes to nothing on the return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' puts the theft inside the musical to give EVITROBA, and 'returning' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abortive means failing to achieve its aim, so unsuccessful or fruitless.

clue.text: Turn old when locked up for comedy? On the contrary

indicators.note: locked up says one word is shut inside the other, as in a cell

parts.note: a turn or go at something is a try
aged means old

explanation.surface: An old prisoner wonders whether being locked up was a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is reversed: the answer is the opposite of comedy, as 'On the contrary' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragedy is the dramatic genre that stands opposite comedy.

clue.text: Criminal chap beds with Mr Ronnie Barker

indicators.note: criminal as an adjective suggests something done wrongly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A crook beds down beside Ronnie Barker, the actor who played Fletcher in Porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Ronnie Barker' reads as one name, but the definition is 'Barker' alone. The anagram uses CHAP BEDS and MR RONNIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dobermann pinscher is a breed of dog, and a dog is a barker.

clue.text: Two characters giving one sound jab that's hit hard

parts.note: a dig is a poke or jab
a rap is a sharp knock or hit
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A punch that lands hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer illustrates itself: its last two letters, PH, are a digraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A digraph is a pair of letters representing a single speech sound, such as sh or ph.

clue.text: See 16
Line from old TV programme

definitions.meaning: a line of descent or succession of rulers from one family
the 1980s American soap opera about the Carrington family

explanation.surface: A line of dialogue from a television show of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of rulers from one family is a lineage, and the same name belonged to a 1980s American soap.

clue.text: One tends to nag youngster on frame

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the second word follows the first in an across answer

parts.note: a horse is a frame or stand, as in a clothes horse or sawhorse
a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: Someone tends to pester a child about their physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb meaning pester; here it is a noun for a horse. 'Tends' means looks after.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseboy is a stable lad who looks after horses, and a nag is an old horse.

clue.text: Content to shop or tour city

indicators.note: content means the stuff held inside, so the answer is lodged within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone happy to go shopping or tour a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy', but it means what the next words hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, Portugal's second city.

clue.text: Protection around grass

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning around
to grass is to inform on someone, which in slang is to sing

explanation.surface: A protective barrier set around a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for informing on someone to the police, as is 'sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A casing is an outer cover that encloses and shields what is inside.

clue.text: Talk following Tory party lines?

indicators.note: following means the first word comes after the second, so the word for Tory goes first

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
gas is idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: Chatter that sticks to the Conservative party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party lines' suggests political policy, but it means lines of dancers at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Congas are dances in which partygoers form a long single-file line.

clue.text: Predetermine Fed's choice of letter? American with it

parts.note: a choice of one letter from the word Fed is F or E or D
in means fashionable or with it

explanation.surface: An American federal agent picks a letter to decide something in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like an FBI agent, but it supplies its letters as alternatives: 'F or E or D'.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreordain is to decree or settle beforehand, which is to predetermine.

clue.text: Choose to sleep around, caught making penetration

indicators.note: making penetration says one letter forces its way inside the other piece
around means the word for sleep is turned back to front

parts.note: kip is British slang for sleep
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A racy line about sleeping around and getting caught in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select or opt for something.

clue.text: See 13
Dry man inside with a foreign letter

indicators.note: inside says the word for man goes within the other piece

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry in the alcohol-free sense
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: A sober man stays indoors with a letter from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a letter from a foreign script.

clue.text: Move back over after time without Norman Stanley Fletcher, initially

indicators.note: after says the rest of the wordplay follows the letter for time
without here means outside, so the turned word surrounds the initials
over means the word for back is turned around

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of these names

explanation.surface: A prison move that goes ahead without Norman Stanley Fletcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Stanley Fletcher is the hero of Porridge. 'Without' means outside here, and 'over' turns the word for back into RAER, which goes round his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer is to move someone or something from one place to another.
